title: Destiny's Clue
content:
Sneha stepped out of Delhi Junction, where the city's endless rhythm welcomed her with blaring horns, bustling crowds, and towering buildings stretching toward the sky. She hailed a cab, settled into the back seat, and silently watched the unfamiliar streets pass by until the vehicle finally stopped in front of a beautiful hotel.

After checking in, she made her way to her room.

The room was quiet and comfortable. She freshened up, changed into casual clothes, and collapsed onto the soft bed. To break the silence, she switched on the television.

But her eyes weren't really watching it.

Her thoughts had wandered elsewhere.

They were with Siddu.

Questions circled endlessly through her mind.

Why had Shreya suddenly disappeared from Siddu's life?

And why had Siddu himself vanished without a word?

The unanswered questions refused to let her mind rest.

Realizing she wouldn't find peace inside the room, Sneha decided to step outside and explore the city.

The evening passed as she wandered through Delhi's lively streets. Crowded markets, historic landmarks, and cheerful faces surrounded her, yet none of it was enough to distract her from the mystery that had become deeply rooted in her heart.

As evening slowly settled over the city, Sneha finally returned to the hotel.

After finishing some office-related work, she walked onto the balcony with a cup of hot tea in her hands. The golden rays of the setting sun painted the sky with shades of orange and crimson, creating a breathtaking view.

For a brief moment, she simply stood there, admiring the sunset.

Just then, her phone vibrated.

The screen displayed a familiar name.

Uncle Venkatesh.

Sneha answered immediately.

"Hello, Uncle."

"I've found the house," he said. "I'm standing outside the house, but it's locked. I'll wait here for a while. If Kiran returns, I'll let you know immediately."

A spark of hope lit up Sneha's face.

"Thank you so much, Uncle."

After ending the call, she waited anxiously.

Every passing minute felt unusually long.

Nearly an hour later, her phone rang again.

She answered it almost instantly.

"Did you meet him?" she asked hopefully.

A brief silence followed.

Then her uncle sighed.

"I waited for quite a while," he said gently. "Later, one of the neighbors told me that he had shifted to another place some time ago. Unfortunately, nobody here knows where he moved."

Sneha's hopeful expression slowly faded.

"I think it's better if you stop searching for him," her uncle continued. "Sometimes, chasing someone who doesn't want to be found only brings more disappointment."

Sneha remained silent for a moment before softly replying,

"Okay, Uncle."

"Don't take it to heart," he said warmly. "You came to Delhi for an important reason. Focus on your career. Everything else will happen at the right time."

A faint smile appeared on Sneha's face.

"You're right, Uncle. Thank you for the advice."

"Take care of yourself."

"You too."

The call ended.

Sneha stood quietly on the balcony, staring at the fading colors of the evening sky.

For a few moments, disappointment weighed heavily on her heart.

Then she slowly took a deep breath.

"I can't change what's already happened," she whispered to herself. "The best thing I can do now is focus on my career."

With that thought, she gathered herself together.

The search for Siddu would have to wait.

The next morning, Sneha woke up before the alarm could ring.

She got ready carefully, dressed in her formal attire, and took one last look at herself in the mirror. Today wasn't just another day—it was the beginning of a new chapter in her life.

After a quick breakfast, she left the hotel and made her way to the company.

The massive glass building stood proudly against the morning sky, reflecting the golden rays of the sun. Employees hurried through the entrance while candidates waited nervously in the reception area.

Sneha took a deep breath and walked inside.

After completing the registration process, she sat quietly in the waiting hall. One by one, candidates were called into the interview room. Some walked out with confident smiles, while others wore expressions of disappointment.

Watching one candidate after another disappear into the interview room only made her heartbeat faster.

To calm herself, she observed the people around her and the professional atmosphere of the office, trying to settle her anxious mind.

Finally, her name echoed through the reception.

"Ms. Sneha."

She stood up, took a deep breath, and walked into the interview room.

The interviewers greeted her warmly before asking her to take a seat.

The conversation began with a few simple introductions and gradually moved on to questions about her education, technical knowledge, projects, and career goals.

Sneha answered each question with confidence.

After the interview concluded, one of the panel members smiled politely.

"Thank you, Sneha. Please wait outside for a few minutes."

She nodded and stepped back into the waiting area.

Those few minutes felt longer than the entire interview.

Finally, one of the interviewers came outside carrying a file.

"Congratulations, Sneha," he said with a smile. "You have been selected. You can report tomorrow for your first day of work."

A wave of happiness rushed through her.

"Thank you, sir," she replied with a grateful smile.

Just as she was about to leave, another interviewer called out to her.

"One more thing."

Sneha turned around.

"Your team leader will be Rohini. She's twenty-five years old and is from Bengaluru. Here's her contact number."

He handed her a small slip of paper.

"You can contact her if you have any questions before joining. That's all. Have a great day."

Sneha thanked the interviewers once again before walking out of the building, holding the slip of paper tightly in her hand.

Little did she know...

The name written on that small piece of paper was about to reconnect her with the mystery she had been trying so desperately to solve.
